title: Arranging for Hines and finding Mundy and Eckstine in Washington
summary: Hines's talent scouting at the Crystal Caverns.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Do you remember what your first arrangement for the band was?
First arrangement for Earl Hines' band, offhand I can't remember.
But did you start arranging as soon as you came into the band?

PROPOSABLE
OPTION CONTENT
Oh, yeah.
He knew that you --
He knew that I could arrange.
And Cecil Irwin did some of the charts?
Cecil Irwin did some of them, Jimmy Mundy.
Yeah. That was a little later when Mundy came in, he came about '33.
When Mundy came in the band -- about '33.
Yeah. But Earl knew he was an arranger before he hired him?
Yeah.
Where did he find all these very talented guys?
Jimmy Mundy we found in the Crystal Caverns in Washington, D. C. That's the same nightclub we found Bill Eckstein.* Also Trummy Young.
In Washington?
In Washington, D. C., yeah.
Well, did they -- did you go out after your gig and, you know, just partying, and hear these people, or --
Yeah. See, we was playing the Howard
*Correct spelling. Changed to "Eckstine" when he became popular in the early 1940s.

Theater, so quite naturally, we got off early, you know. And just going around to different nightclubs, you know, when you get off. And we heard Jimmy Mundy and Trummy Young, and said, well, that's it. Earl said, that's it.
So Jimmy was hired first for his playing, and then for --
For his arranging.
He certainly turned into a great arranger.
Yeah, he did a lot of arranging. Benny Goodman's --
I think that 'Sing, Sing --
The 'Benny Goodman Story.'
'Sing, Sing, Sing,' he did the arrangement on that. I think.
I think, I don't know. I'm not for sure. He did a lot of arranging --
That's a hell of a piece of music.
After he left Earl, he went out freelancing, did a lot of arrangements for Benny Goodman. In fact, that's how he wound up out on the Coast.
Good tenor man, too.
Writing for pictures.
Good player.
Yeah.
